question: Why does the application browser suite fail under WebKit?
method: Playwright WebKit/Chromium/Firefox from .toolchain, against the development server on this machine; the dev sign-in, then the suite harness page, then a storage probe.
findings: The session is fine in all three engines: /api/v1/me answers 200 with the same deviceId, so DEVICE_REQUIRED was not a session or cookie problem.
On the harness page, Chromium builds a fixture; WebKit refuses with BYTE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE.

Storage probe: in this WebKit build navigator.storage.getDirectory() throws UnknownError ("operation failed for an unknown transient reason"); IndexedDB opens normally. Chromium and Firefox return an OPFS root and pass the write probe.
productBehaviour: src/storage/bytes.mjs categorises that failure as policy-or-io-blocked, which the application policy (fallbackWhen: unsupported, verification-failed) deliberately does not treat as a reason to fall back to IndexedDB: silently moving to a second store could strand what is already in OPFS and look like lost projects. The refusal is by design; only the sentence the person reads was missing, and is now in DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT.
notVerified: Whether desktop Safari behaves like this Playwright WebKit build. No Safari on this machine. Nothing here is a claim about Safari.
consequence: The WebKit run of tests/app/run.ps1 cannot open a store, so its cases fail for that reason, not for the behaviour they test.
whatThePersonSees: The start screen loads normally in WebKit; creating a project is refused with "Không tạo được dự án" and, after this round, a Vietnamese sentence explaining that the browser will not let the application open its own file store and why it does not silently use a second one (webkit-store-refusal-1440.png).

browserSuiteRun.command: tests/app/run.ps1 -Seat codex -Browsers webkit, on this round's commit
browserSuiteRun.reading: The application works in this WebKit build for 44 of 46 behaviours. OPFS fails its own write-close-read probe (0 bytes back), the store files that as verification-failed, and the policy does allow the IndexedDB fallback for that category, which is why the suite runs at all. Two cases end on a different error code than Chromium, and the offline lease has no Ed25519 here.
browserSuiteRun.correction: An earlier note in this project said the WebKit run failed 23 cases with DEVICE_REQUIRED. That is not reproducible on this commit and is withdrawn: the session and device id are healthy in WebKit, and the storage path is what differs.
